newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada spot natural gas sinks as temperatures rise.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot natural gas sinks as temperatures rise.

text.p: Most Canadian spot natural gas prices were sharply lower in Wednesday trade, especially those in the key Alberta market where temperatures were forecast to be mild through the weekend.

Spot gas at the AECO storage hub was talked at C$2.68/2.70 per gigajoule, down about two cents from last week but off as much as 44 cents from Tuesday trade. Gas for February delivery sank to C$2.67 per GJ, down from C$2.85 on January 22.
"I don't see any upside here before the end of the weekend," said a Calgary-based marketer who added that previously frozen production units were coming back on stream.
Environment Canada said temperatures in southern Alberta were forecast to hover around the freezing point at least until Sunday.

Above-normal temperatures were also expected in British Columbia and the U.S. Pacific Northwest, which led to softer gas prices at Sumas, Wash. Traders said Sumas gas was discussed between US$2.20 and US$2.42 per million British thermal units, down about a dime on average from last week.

Eastern Canadian prices, however, continued an upward trend as southern Ontario and the U.S. Northeast braced for colder weather. Gas at Niagara was quoted at US$3.35/3.45 per mmBtu, up about one cent from Tuesday and 40 cents from last week. February Niagara was said to be trading in the low US$3.40s.
